content:
Apple today unveiled its latest Mac mini and Mac Studio models, alongside minor updates to its lineup of Magic Keyboard accessories.

The latest Magic Keyboard replaces text labels on keys with icons.

Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio feature new-generation M6 chips and the high-end M5 Ultra, delivering significant performance improvements.

You can now pre-order the latest models: Mac mini here, and Mac Studio here.

Beyond the desktop upgrades, Apple has also refreshed the Magic Keyboard range, with a subtle change to the new models.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes text labels from several keys in favor of icon symbols.

Apple introduced the same change earlier this year on the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, and MacBook Pro, and the Magic Keyboard now follows suit.

This change applies to all new Magic Keyboard models:

  • Magic Keyboard: $99
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID: $149
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad: $179

Commonly used keys such as tab, caps lock, return, shift, and delete have switched from text labels to icon-only designs. On the extended models with a numeric keypad, keys like Home, Page Up, and Page Down have also been replaced with new icons instead of the original text.

Aside from the switch to icons, the new Magic Keyboard looks identical to the previous generation, continuing to support USB-C with the same features and layout.

What are your thoughts on the removal of text labels from the keys? Share your views in the comments section.
